title: Cross-stitch sunflower motif
subtitle: A bold sunflower head in yellow and brown on 14-count navy Aida
excerpt: A large single sunflower head in golden yellows and warm browns on 14-count navy Aida. The design is approximately 70 by 70 stitches and finishes at about 12 by 12 cm. The navy background provides all the contrast the yellow petals need and makes the finished piece vivid without added background stitching.
sourceNotes: Original design. The sunflower (Helianthus annuus) is native to North America and widely grown in UK gardens. Cross-stitch on coloured Aida is a standard approach in UK needlework publishing that removes the need for background fill stitching.

content.text: Coloured Aida does the work of a background so you stitch only the flower. The petal ring and the disc fill are the two main sections; both use simple cross-stitch fill with no specialist stitches needed.

items.label: Thread
items.value: DMC 3820 (dark straw), 3821 (straw), 3822 (light straw), 972 (deep canary), 3856 (ultra very light mahogany), 3857 (dark rosewood), 433 (brown), 434 (light brown)

content.text: Each petal is elongated and roughly six by twelve stitches. Fill the outer two-thirds of each petal in 3822 (lightest) and the inner third in 3821, with a small zone of 3820 at the base where the petal meets the disc.
Fill the disc in concentric zones.

The centre disc is roughly circular, about twenty-two stitches across. Work the outer ring of the disc in 433 (brown), the middle ring in 3857, and the inner zone in 3856. Add a small cluster of 3820 yellow stitches at the very centre.
Work a single back-stitch line down the centre of each petal in 3820 using one strand. This gives the petals the characteristic sunflower vein structure.
One strand of 433 in back-stitch defines where the petal ring meets the disc.
Frame in a 15 × 15 cm square frame or display in a 15 cm hoop. The navy Aida works equally well as a hoop frame or behind a white card mount in a picture frame.
